outcome.description: The data arrives in a compressed burst: months of shipping records, cross-referenced with Guild manifests and black market movement logs. The pattern is damning: every major weapons shipment to pirate groups in the last year was routed through three specific Guild logistics hubs, all managed by the same administrative department. Section Nine. The name keeps surfacing. Your contact adds a personal note: 'Burn this after you read it. These people make pirates look civilized.'

Your contact considers the offer, then agrees. You share the weapons serial data and courier manifest; they send you their shipping analysis. The combined intelligence paints a picture of an operation far larger than a few corrupt officials: The Ledger has been running parallel supply chains across the entire Expanse for years. Your contact's parting words: 'We're both targets now. At least we're informed targets.'
Your contact shrugs over the comm. 'Your call, Captain. But this data has a shelf life. Once they rotate their routes, and they will, it's worthless.' The channel closes.

Uncle Szabo loads two drums into your hold with a gap-toothed grin. 'Now, she might smell a little funny at first, but once she heats up? Smooth as silk. My grandmother's recipe. Well, she used it for soup, but the principle's the same.'
Szabo talks your ear off for twenty minutes about coolant chemistry, his grandmother's soup, and a fish he once caught on Verdant that was 'big as a shuttle, I swear it.'
Szabo scratches his chin. '{Son}, I been running this route since before your ship was scrap metal. But I appreciate the concern.' He putters off, unbothered.

You match course with Reeta, broadcasting routine trade chatter. The patrol shadow loses interest in a two-ship convoy and peels off. Reeta exhales. 'People at Haven's Rest clinic needed this a week ago. You just helped more folks than you know.' She sends over a cut of her payment.
Reeta sells you a crate of medical supplies at cost, well below what any station pharmacy charges. 'Sell it, use it, give it away. I don't care. Just don't tell the Guild where you got it.'
Reeta nods curtly and accelerates away. 'Understood. No judgment. Everybody's got their own line.' Her ship vanishes into the lane traffic.
You dock in silence. Nobody exchanges names. The goods are quality. You pay a fraction of market rate and part ways with a nod.
You memorize their heading and vessel profile. A Guild patrol would pay for this kind of tip. The smuggler vanishes into the dark, oblivious.
You send a single character reply: 'N.' The freighter kills its tight-beam and drifts away without a sound.

The transfer is quick and quiet. The panels are exactly as described: pristine mil-spec plating with a tiny stamp reading 'REJECTED: cosmetic.' You can sell these anywhere outside Forgeworks for a healthy profit. The worker vanishes back into the station's traffic pattern without a trace.

You relay the shuttle's ID and frequency to Crucible Station security. The worker scrambles, but the shuttle is too slow to outrun a patrol. Station management sends you a modest informant's reward. The worker's coworkers won't thank you for this, but the books will balance.
You wave the shuttle off. The worker mutters something about 'management bootlickers' and drifts away. The panels will probably end up in someone else's cargo bay by tomorrow.
